full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 236

HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. v. TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd.
— Dispute over liability for vessel collision damage

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on November 25, 2024)

Keywords
civil; liability for vessel collision damage; foreign-related; agreement on choice of law; applicable law

Ruling Gist

Pursuant to Article 44 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, where the parties to a foreign-related dispute over liability for vessel collision damage agree on the choice of law after the occurrence of the collision, the applicable law for the dispute shall be determined in accordance with their agreement.

Basic Facts

On September 27, 2022, the "Moufeng" (a Panamanian-flag oil tanker) owned by TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd., while overtaking the "Mouya" (a Liberian-flag container vessel) owned by HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as HuanMou Ship Company) in the Strait of Malacca, collided with the latter due to a steering gear failure and improper maneuvering of the "Moufeng." In December 2022, HuanMou Ship Company applied to the Ningbo Maritime Court for the arrest of the "Moufeng," which was then under repair at the Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan, and filed a lawsuit in January 2023, seeking an order that TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. compensate for hull damage, loss of hire, and other losses totaling RMB 58,108,824.77 plus interest. TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. filed a counterclaim, seeking an order that HuanMou Ship Company compensate for its various losses totaling RMB 38,115,057.62 plus interest. The Ningbo Maritime Court consolidated the main action and the counterclaim. During the trial, both the plaintiff and the defendant unanimously chose to apply Chinese law.

Judgment

The Ningbo Maritime Court tried the case by applying Chinese law and on February 7, 2024, rendered the civil judgment (2023) Zhe 72 Min Chu No. 314: 1. TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. shall compensate HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. for losses in the amount of RMB 37,182,079.93; 2. HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. shall compensate TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. for losses in the amount of RMB 3,094,472.96; 3. After the setoff of the above two amounts, TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. for losses in the amount of RMB 34,087,606.97 plus interest losses; 4. TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. the pre-litigation preservation application fee of RMB 4,500; 5. The remaining claims of HuanMou Ship Leasing Co., Ltd. are rejected; 6. The remaining counterclaims of TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. are rejected. After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, the judgment became legally effective, and TianMou Wealth Co., Ltd. has voluntarily performed the obligations under the judgment.

Reasoning

This case is a foreign-related dispute over liability for vessel collision damage. The Ningbo Maritime Court, upon the application of HuanMou Ship Company and in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, arrested the "Moufeng." Article 19 of that Law provides: "After the enforcement of maritime claim preservation, if the relevant maritime dispute has not entered litigation or arbitration proceedings, the party concerned may, regarding such maritime claim, file a lawsuit with the maritime court that adopted the maritime claim preservation or with any other maritime court having jurisdiction, unless the parties have entered into a litigation jurisdiction agreement or an arbitration agreement." HuanMou Ship Company accordingly filed a lawsuit with the Ningbo Maritime Court, and the Ningbo Maritime Court has jurisdiction over this case.

Article 273, paragraph 1 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China provides: "The law of the place where the tort is committed shall apply to the compensation for damages caused by collision of ships." Article 44 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations provides: "Tort liability shall be governed by the law of the place where the tort is committed, but if the parties have a common habitual residence, the law of that common habitual residence shall apply. After the occurrence of the tort, if the parties agree on the choice of law, their agreement shall prevail." Although the Maritime Code, as a special law, does not explicitly provide that parties to a vessel collision dispute may choose the applicable law, the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations clearly provides for the parties' choice of law applicable to tort liability. Therefore, the choice of law by the parties in a vessel collision dispute does not constitute a circumstance where the choice is invalid. In the present case, both parties are companies registered in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the flag states of the two vessels involved are Panama and Liberia, respectively. During the trial, the plaintiff and the defendant unanimously submitted that Chinese law should apply to the tort liability dispute in this case. Since the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations has clearly provided for the parties' agreement on the choice of law applicable to tort liability, it shall be determined that the choice of Chinese law by both the plaintiff and the defendant in this case is valid.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 3 and Article 44 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations
Article 273 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China
Article 19 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China
